note: The accelerator runaway is RESOLVED, and the cause was the cold-plate MODEL, not the GA100 power map. Supersedes the conclusion in accelerator_water_envelope.json, which read a finned-water-block result as a property of the die.
what_was_wrong: CoolingSpec's water path builds a FINNED BASE sized for the die -- a water block. On the 826 mm^2 GA100 it returns 0.055 K/W and bottoms its own flow solver out at a face velocity it then flags as unbuildable. On that boundary the die has no steady state above ~250 W, which is why every accelerator point in the first re-run attempt returned RUNAWAY. A direct-die accelerator is not cooled by a water block.
the_fix: sink_models.MicrochannelSink -- a direct-die microchannel cold plate anchored on a MEASURED reference: 1020 W/cm^2 background flux dissipated at <69 C above inlet and <120 kPa, at a channel mass flux of 2100 kg/(m^2 s), with hotspot fluxes to 2700 W/cm^2 raising the hotspot only 16 C. Channels are 15-33 um wide and 35-470 um deep, etched into the back of the die.

comparison.comment: The GA100 at full H100-class power is comfortable on a real cold plate: 64 C at 700 W. It had no steady state at 300 W on the water block. The catalogue can therefore keep its real operating points (400 and 700 W) rather than being re-centred onto an envelope that was an artefact of the sink model.

pump_power.caveat: Channels ONLY -- a floor. The manifold, plenum and facility loop are not modelled. For scale, the LCEstimator CDU figure is ~7 W per device for the whole loop (13.7 kW electrical over ~1950 devices at nominal), so the channels are a small part of it. The flow here (1.7e-05 m^3/s) is close to the CDU per-device nominal (1.0e-05), which is the cross-check that matters.
pump_power.note: The reference rig runs a ~2 K fluid rise, far more flow than a practical loop. r_conv is held flow-independent because microchannel flow is deeply laminar and developed-laminar Nu is a constant of the geometry; only the caloric term moves with flow.

what_this_does_not_model: manifold and plenum pressure drop, flow maldistribution across channels, fouling, and the thermal interface between the channel wafer and the die. All of those make a real plate worse.
